Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comentario: GB409_5 was blank (no value annotated). Henderson (2013:13) states: 'In nominals other than pronouns Nominative and Accusative are syncretised' — meaning full NPs have a distinct Ergative case (separate from NOM/ACC syncretism). This is consistent with GB409_2=1 (1sg ERG≠NOM), GB409_3=0, GB409_4=0 (other pronouns syncretise ERG/NOM). Value set to 1. Source: Henderson 2013:13. Note: Wilkins (1989) would provide additional confirmation with paradigm tables but is not available as a PDF in this archive.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 0. Absolutive (S and O) is zero-marked in Gurung. Table 4 (p.74) and Fig.14 (p.77) show Intransitive Subject: UM (unmarked) and Transitive Object: UM (unmarked). Glover describes the system as "nominative-ergative" (p.71), meaning A is ergative-marked and S/O are zero. Case table (p.70): Ergative=-d, with no absolutive suffix listed. Source: Glover 1974:70-74.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. 1sg pronoun Qa/Ia- takes ergative -d in transitive clauses: "Qa-d ... ax-ca-syo" (me-ER not-eat-EM, p.82 ex.42); "Ia-dl ... bo-la" (me-ER take-PLUP, p.77 ex.24). Source: Glover 1974:82,77.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. 2sg pronoun kxl takes ergative -d in transitive and imperative contexts: "kxl-d ax-bl-le tl-Ql-d" (you-ER ... stay-IM, p.85 ex.49); also kxl-d in ex.85 p.85. Source: Glover 1974:85,30.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative marking occurs in non-past (imperfective) tenses. Ex.26 (p.77-78): "Ixy6-d ca ka'gada Ixyo-m" (we.INCL-ER that paper look.at-NP) with nonpast -m. Ex.27 (p.78): "bomw~-d puja la-m" (Brahmin-ER worship do-NP) with nonpast -m. Source: Glover 1974:77-78.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative marking occurs in perfective/past tenses. Ex.24 (p.77): "Ia-dl ... bo-la" (me-ER take-PLUP); ex.43 (p.83): "a99a-d cha'b thaudi-f" (office-ER stamp affix-PA). Source: Glover 1974:77,82-83.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative marking occurs consistently in past tenses. Multiple examples with past (-l, -i) and pluperfect (-la): ex.24 "Ia-dl bo-la" (me-ER take-PLUP, p.77); ex.43 "a99a-d thaudi-f" (office-ER affix-PA, p.83). Source: Glover 1974:77-83.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative marking occurs in non-past tenses. Ex.26 (p.77-78): "Ixy6-d ka'gada Ixyo-m" (we.INCL-ER paper look.at-NP); ex.27 (p.78): "bomw~-d puja la-m" (Brahmin-ER do-NP). Both use nonpast suffix -m with ergative-marked agent. Source: Glover 1974:77-78.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative -d appears in non-indicative (imperative) forms. Ex.49 (p.85): "kxl-d ax-bl-le tl-Ql-d" (you-ER [without-saying-anything] stay-IM) uses the imperative suffix -d with ergative-marked 2sg. The ergative is a CASE marker applied to the transitive/causative subject regardless of mood. Source: Glover 1974:85.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative marking is a case property of transitive subjects, not conditioned by realis/irrealis status. Glover's categorical statement (p.76): "ergative for the Transitive Clause." Ex.29 (p.122): "l~ma-d ... ax-cxu-m~la" (lama-ER not-prepare-PLUP.HAB) shows ergative with habituative -mala (modal/irrealis-adjacent). The unreal -mala (apodosis of hypotheticals, ex.27) has OCR-ambiguous text but no exception stated in the grammar. Source: Glover 1974:74,77,122.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. Non-agentive A (Instrument, Non-instigative Cause) takes ergative -d. Table 4 (p.74) lists Transitive Subject roles as "A, C, AX" where C = Non-instigative Cause; all take ER marking. Ex.25 (p.77-78): "n~'-d ... p~'-l" (rain-ER soak-PA) — rain is Non-instigative Cause; book p.30 states Instrumental is "realized identically with -d". Source: Glover 1974:30,74,77-78.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. Non-topical agents take ergative. The vast majority of ergative-marked agents in the corpus carry no topic particle: ex.25 "n~'-d" (rain-ER), ex.43 "a99a-d" (office-ER), ex.27 "bomw~-d" (Brahmin-ER), all without topic marking. Crucially, in ex.51-52 (pp.84-85), agents take BOTH ergative AND topic marker simultaneously (-d-am = ER+TOPIC), confirming ergative is not replaced by topic-marking. Source: Glover 1974:82-85.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. Inanimate agents take ergative -d. Ex.25 (p.77-78): "n~'-d ... p~'-l" (rain-ER soak-PA); ex.43 (p.83): "a99a-d cha'b thaudi-f" (office-ER stamp affix-PA). Both are inanimate Non-instigative Causes/Agents with ergative marking. Source: Glover 1974:77-78,83.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 1. Ergative is a case-marking property not restricted to main clauses. Glover (p.71) describes -d as a "postposition" (case clitic) in the Relator system, applied to the subject of Transitive Clauses (Table 4, p.74). No restriction to main clause distribution is stated. Subordinate clause examples (gerund -ba, relative -bae) typically show deleted/implicit agents (contextually recoverable); no exception to ergative marking is noted for non-main clauses. Source: Glover 1974:71-74.

Descripción_rasgo: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 0. Ergative alignment is not conditioned by any additional factor beyond transitivity. Glover's categorical description: "ergative for the Transitive Clause" (p.76), "unmarked for the Loc-Intransitive" (p.76). The ergative suffix -d applies consistently to all transitive subjects (Agent, Instrument/Cause, Agent-Experiencer) across tenses, aspects, and moods. No split conditioning (tense, person, animacy, topicality) is described. Source: Glover 1974:70-78.

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 0. Ergative suffix -d is distinct from the genitive -e (possessive/genitive). Case table (p.70) lists: Ergative=-d, Genitive=-e (or -a/-'(a)). These are formally distinct markers. Source: Glover 1974:70.

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Original value ? resolved to 0. Ergative suffix -d is distinct from the comitative -ne/-na. Case table (p.70) lists: Ergative=-d, Comitative=-ne/-na as separate case markers. Source: Glover 1974:70.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comentario: Original value 0 is incorrect. Van den Berg (1995:42) section 3.4.2 explicitly introduces the ergative case with full NP examples in PRESENT tense: ol-di-l m-uq es (boy-OBL-ERG eat-PRES apple) 'the boy eats an apple'; wexa-l-lo n-uq xo (shepherd-OBL-ERG eat-PRES meat). Section 6.4.2 (p.122-123) confirms Agent+Patient [ERG, NOM] as the standard transitive pattern with full NP examples: ol-di-l kid hehe-r (boy-OBL-ERG girl hit-PRET); iyu-l hcxrac b-oho-r (mother-ERG cow feed-PRET). Full NPs take the ergative suffix -l (after vowel/y) or -lo (after consonant) on the oblique stem. Value corrected to 1. Source: Van den Berg 1995:42-43, 122-123.

Descripción_rasgo: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comentario: REVERT: The original value 0 is correct. A batch-correction had changed this to 1, premised on a tense-based split (GB409_8=1 past vs. GB409_9=0 non-past). PDF verification (Van den Berg 1995:84-86) shows that GB409_9=0 was itself incorrect — ERG marking applies in aorist, future, and intentional forms (see GB409_9 correction). Since ERG is not conditioned by tense or any other factor identified in the grammar, value 0 is confirmed. Reverted batch-correction to 0.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Hurrian ergative case (-š) is not conditioned by aspect. The imperfective/future aspect (suffix -et-, Wegner 2007:86-87) uses the same ergative marking as other aspects. Table 1 (pp.64-65) shows no aspect conditioning. Source: Wegner 2007:64-65, 86-87.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Perfective/preterite aspect (suffix -os-, Wegner 2007:86-87) shows the same ergative alignment. Ergative (-š) marks A consistently. Source: Wegner 2007:64-65, 86-87.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Preterite (past) tense forms show ergative alignment; preterite uses perfective aspect suffix -os-. Ergative (-š) applies in past tense. Source: Wegner 2007:64-65, 86-87.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Present/non-past tense (null aspect marker, Wegner 2007:86) also shows ergative alignment. Ergative is not conditioned by tense. Source: Wegner 2007:64-65, 86-87.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Non-indicative forms (Jussiv/jussive, section 5.6, Wegner 2007:102-103) also show the transitive/intransitive (ergative/absolutive) distinction. Ergative alignment extends to non-indicative moods. Source: Wegner 2007:102-103.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Realis (indicative) forms consistently show ergative alignment (GB409_10=1 already confirmed). Source: Wegner 2007:64-65, 94.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Irrealis/non-indicative forms (jussive section 5.6, Wegner 2007:102-103) also show the transitive-ergative distinction. Ergative alignment applies in irrealis contexts. Source: Wegner 2007:102-103.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Ergative marks all A arguments in transitive sentences. No restriction to agentive A is mentioned. Source: Wegner 2007:64-67.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. The grammar (Wegner 2007:66-67) defines the ergative as "Subjektkasus in transitiven objekthaltigen Sätzen" (subject case in transitive sentences with object) without any restriction to agentive A. No evidence of absolutive marking for non-agentive A (e.g., experiencer subjects) in this source. Source: Wegner 2007:64-67.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. No topicality conditioning of the ergative case is mentioned in Wegner (2007). Ergative marks all A arguments regardless of topicality. Source: Wegner 2007:64-67.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. No topicality conditioning mentioned; ergative applies uniformly. Source: Wegner 2007:64-67.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. No animacy hierarchy for ergative marking mentioned in Wegner (2007). Animate A takes ergative. Source: Wegner 2007:64-67.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. No animacy conditioning mentioned; ergative applies to both animate and inanimate A arguments. Source: Wegner 2007:64-67.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Main clause ergative alignment confirmed by all cited examples. Source: Wegner 2007:64-67.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Ergative case marking persists in subordinate/relative clauses. The relative pronoun is always absolutive (Wegner 2007:84-85) because it relativizes the absolutive position, but full NPs in transitive subordinate clauses still take ergative. Source: Wegner 2007:84-85.

Descripción_rasgo: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comentario: Resolved to 0. Hurrian ergative is not conditioned by any additional factor beyond standard transitivity (presence of object). The ergative applies uniformly regardless of tense, aspect, mood, animacy, or topicality. The antipassive construction (absolutive for A without object) is standard ergative behavior, not a split. Source: Wegner 2007:64-67.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comentario: Iaai has no ergative alignment. Ozanne-Rivierre (1976:148-149) §4.37-4.39: PERSONNELS 1 (agent) mark ALL subjects — both S of intransitives and A of transitives (same forms for attributive/stative and active subjects). PERSONNELS 2 (objet) mark objects. §4.3 (p.133): lexical NPs appear in unmarked form postposed to the verb. Transitivity is marked on the verb, not on NP arguments (§4.8, p.134). The label '(agent)' refers to semantic role, not to an ergative/absolutive distinction. Value changed from '?' to 0.

Ozanne-Rivierre (1976:148-149) §4.37-4.39: PERSONNELS 1 (agent) mark ALL subjects — both S of intransitives and A of transitives (same forms for attributive/stative and active subjects). PERSONNELS 2 (objet) mark objects. §4.3 (p.133): lexical NPs appear in unmarked form postposed to the verb. Transitivity is marked on the verb, not on NP arguments (§4.8, p.134). The label '(agent)' refers to semantic role, not to an ergative/absolutive distinction. Value changed from '?' to 0.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comentario: Ilongot has ergative-absolutive alignment (Philippine focus system). NOM marker ma marks absolutive NPs (patient of transitive + S of intransitive). Liao (2008:3) ex.(4): kinan ni Madiya ma manok = ate GEN.Maria NOM.chicken ("Maria ate the chicken"). ma is overt ABS marker.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comentario: GEN pronoun =ko (1sg agent) vs NOM =/(C)ak (1sg S/O). Liao (2008:5-6) Table 1 and §4.2.2: NOM pronoun functions as S of intransitive (ex.14), agent of dyadic intransitive (ex.15), AND theme/patient of transitive (ex.16). GEN =ko marks transitive agent. Ergative alignment on 1sg.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comentario: GEN pronoun =mo (2sg agent) vs NOM =ka (2sg S/O). Liao (2008:5-6) Table 1 and §4.2.2. Same pattern as 1sg. Ergative alignment on 2sg.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comentario: GEN pronoun =to/=tu (3sg agent) vs no NOM 3sg form (zero/absent). Liao (2008:5-6) Table 1: 3sg NOM is "---" (no form). Ex.(16): kadɨvaan=tu=(v)ak (accompany=GEN.3SG=NOM.1SG) "She will accompany me" — 3sg agent uses GEN. Ergative alignment present on 3sg (agent marked by GEN).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comentario: Full NP: ni (GEN, agent marker) vs ma (NOM, patient/S marker). Liao (2008:3) ex.(4): kinan ni Madiya ma manok noy mase (ate GEN.Maria NOM.chicken last.night) "Maria ate the chicken last night." Overt ergative-absolutive alignment on full NPs.

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: ERG=GEN: The ergative/agent marker IS the genitive marker in Ilongot. Liao (2008:4) §4.2.1: "the genitive pronoun in Ilongot is used as a nominal modifier AND as the agent of a transitive clause." Full NP: ni is both genitive and agent marker. Pronoun series: GEN (=ko, =mo, =to etc.) functions both as possessive and transitive agent.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comentario: Original value 0 is incorrect. Jacques (2004:464) example (340) shows full NP with ERG suffix -kə: tə-rmi-ndʒês-kə (homme-duel-ERG) as transitive agent. P.465 confirms: 'l'actant marqué à l'ergatif des verbes transitifs' (the participant marked in the ergative of transitive verbs). Note: citing p.464 for both GB409_4=1 and GB409_5=0 is internally inconsistent. Value corrected to 1. Source: Jacques 2004:464-465.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comentario: Original value 0 is incorrect. Applebaum (2013:77) Table 3.25 'Summary of case marking in Kabardian' explicitly shows: common nouns ERG=-m, ABS=-r. Common nouns take the same ergative marker -m as 3rd person singular pronouns. Note: proper nouns are ERG=0 (unmarked), but common nouns have overt ERG flagging. Value corrected to 1. Source: Applebaum 2013:77, Table 3.25.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comentario: Original value "?" resolved to 0. Free pronouns (dIkará̩ "I", kai "you", Ʌ́kɪ "s/he") are the same for S (intransitive subject) and A (transitive subject) — nominative pattern. Pronominal objects are obligatorily incorporated into the verb, not free pronouns with case marking. No ergative-absolutive distinction exists on 1st person pronouns. Source: Ribeiro 2012:174 (nominative agreement), 191-192 (pronominal objects incorporated).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comentario: Original value "?" resolved to 0. Third person free pronoun Ʌ́kɪ "s/he" is used for both intransitive S and transitive A (nominative pattern). Third person objects are incorporated into the verb. Source: Ribeiro 2012:174, 191-192.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comentario: Original value "?" resolved to 0. Full NPs show no overt case marking. Example: ha̩bu ha̩lOkOE 3-CTFG-TRANS-kill-PERF "The man killed the jaguar" — both NPs are zero-marked, distinguished only by position. Source: Ribeiro 2012:51.

Descripción_rasgo: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comentario: Original value 0 is likely incorrect. No source reference provided. Gawne (2016:67-68) explicitly states: "The optionality of ergative case-marking depends on a number of factors; those that I discuss below include agentivity, tense and habitual mood." Ergativity in Lamjung Yolmo is conditioned by agentivity (high-agentivity A more likely to take ERG) and tense (more frequent in past tense). This constitutes conditioning by other factors. Corrected to 1. Source: Gawne 2016:67-68.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comentario: Original value 1 is incorrect. Plaisier (2010:127-129) explicitly states that animacy of the subject is one of the key factors conditioning -nun~-nu: the marker is used "when an animate agent and an animate patient are linked by a transitive verb" and the factors include "animacy of the subject." Inanimate A arguments do not receive ergative marking in Lepcha. Corrected to 0. Source: Plaisier 2010:127-129.

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Original value was empty. Based on Plaisier (2010:127-129): the ergative marker is -nun~-nu (ABL suffix in dual function), while the genitive is expressed by -sa (visible in Ex.242: hudo-sa "3S.OBL-GEN" and Ex.243: hudo-sa daughter-ABL). ERG and GEN are expressed by distinct morphemes. Value set to 0. Source: Plaisier 2010:127-129.

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Original value 1 is incorrect for modern standard Lezgian. Haspelmath (1993:84) explicitly states: "this construction is never used in the modern language, where the instrumental function is expressed by the Superelative or Superessive cases." The cited example (144) is archaic/obsolete. The ERG and instrumental markers are synchronically distinct. Corrected to 0.

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Original value 0 is incorrect. Van Driem (1987:34) explicitly lists ergative <-?ille, -le>, instrumental <-?ille, -le>, and genitive <-?ille, -le> as the same morpheme. The ERG suffix -le/-re and GEN suffix -re are allomorphs of a single oblique marker — a well-documented feature of Tibeto-Burman languages. Corrected to 1. Source: Van Driem 1987:34.

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Original value 0 is incorrect. Van Driem (1987:34) explicitly lists ergative <-?ille, -le> and instrumental <-?ille, -le> as the same morpheme (along with genitive). Corrected to 1. Source: Van Driem 1987:34.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comentario: Original "?" resolved to 1. Table 1 (Arka 2012:152) lists 2SG ka with undergoer prefix k- on the verb. The =i absolutive clitic marks all U arguments (P and patientive S) regardless of person. While no direct ka=i example is cited, the paradigm is systematic (1SG na=i confirmed in examples 3a, 5b). Source: Arka 2012:152-153.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comentario: Original "?" resolved to 1. Table 1 (Arka 2012:152) shows 3SG efi and 3NonSG emnde with zero undergoer prefix on verb (Ø), but the =i clitic still attaches to the U pronoun/NP itself. This is confirmed by full-NP examples such as Robertus=i, Maria=i (example 6, p.154). 3rd person U NPs take =i. Source: Arka 2012:152-154.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. The =i absolutive marker is not conditioned by aspect. Examples across different aspect/tense contexts show consistent =i marking on U arguments. Source: Arka 2012:153-154.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Perfective examples: tamba=na Robertus=i ... feri (already=1SG Robertus=U ... give.RPST, ex.6a p.154). =i present with remote past (perfective). Source: Arka 2012:154.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. Present/non-past example: daka=i taw=Ø-ramon (water=U take=3-AUX.1NonPL.PST, ex.7b p.154) and di Ø-nda-Ø (NPST, ex.7a). The =i marking is not conditioned by tense. Source: Arka 2012:154.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comentario: Resolved to 1. All attested examples with =i are in the indicative mood. Source: Arka 2012:153-154.

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Resolved to 0. There is no distinct ERGATIVE case marker in Marori. Transitive A (actor) is zero-marked; the language uses an ABSOLUTIVE marker =i (not ergative marking). Genitive/possessive uses a different marker (=na/=n for beneficiary, p.154). Source: Arka 2012:152-154.

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comentario: 1st person agent takes ergative marker -te in transitive clauses: ex. (85) 'Ã -te mã ax' (1sg.AG ERG eat FUT) = 'Eu comerei'. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:146, ex.85).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comentario: By paradigmatic analogy with 1st and 3rd person: -te marks transitive agents across person categories. No direct 2nd person example found in available pages; requires additional verification of Campos 2009.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comentario: 3rd person NPs and pronominal A arguments take ergative marker -te: ex. (50) 'Ũn -te kakxop xi-nãhã' (woman ERG boy eat-CAUS), (53) 'Tik -te xapup kup-nag-ãhã' (man ERG pig bone-thin-CAUS). Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comentario: Full NPs in A (transitive agent) position consistently take ergative marker -te; S (intransitive subjects) lack -te. Classic ergative flagging. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3, examples 50-65).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comentario: No imperfective/perfective split documented in available pages; -te appears consistently. Corrected from 0 to 1 pending verification of aspect conditioning in Campos 2009.

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comentario: Perfective transitive clauses (completed events) consistently show -te on A (examples 50-65). Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comentario: Past/completed transitive clauses show -te on A throughout examples 50-65. No tense split documented. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comentario: Future (non-past) transitive clause shows -te: ex. (85) 'Ã -te mã ax' (1sg.AG ERG eat FUT). No tense-based split. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:146, ex.85).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comentario: Indicative mood transitive clauses consistently show -te on A. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3, examples 50-65).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comentario: Future/non-indicative transitive clause shows -te: ex. (85) 'Ã -te mã ax' (1sg.AG ERG eat FUT). No mood split. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:146, ex.85).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comentario: Realis transitive clauses show -te on A throughout examples 50-65. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comentario: Future marker -ax corresponds to non-realis/irrealis; transitive future clause (85) shows -te on A. Corrected from 0 to 1, requires verification of full irrealis paradigm (Campos 2009:146, ex.85).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comentario: Agentive A arguments consistently take -te: ex. (50) woman feeds boy, (53) man fattens pig, (63) grandmother makes food. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comentario: Animate A arguments (human agents) take -te throughout examples 50-65. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comentario: Inanimate A argument attested with -te: ex. (57) 'Yip -te kuxa-nõ-a kãmãnok' (car ERG heart-end-CAUS horse) = 'o carro assustou o cavalo'. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:140, ex.57).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comentario: Main clauses consistently show -te on transitive agents throughout §8.1.3. Corrected from 0 to 1 (Campos 2009:§8.1.3).

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comentario: Agentive A (transitive agent with volitional control) consistently takes the ergative marker 'ni' throughout the document. The canonical transitive constructions documented in Santiago (2013) all involve agentive A with ergative marking. Source: Santiago 2013: 5-7

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comentario: Ergative marking on non-topical A (marker 'ni') applies in subordinate and nominalized constructions documented in Santiago (2013), consistent with the general Philippine-type system. Source: Santiago 2013: 17-19

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comentario: Experiencer/non-agentive predicates (fear, hear) are INTRANSITIVE in Akuntsu; their single argument takes the absolutive dependent clitic, not the ergative independent pronoun (e=pip 'you are afraid', o=apinom 'I hear'). Corrected from original value of 1. Source: Aragon 2014: 181, 196

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comentario: Inanimate A takes the ergative marker {-at}: comején (termite)-ERG, p.186 ex.6.7b. Original annotation was '?' due to absence of explicit examples; PDF verification confirms inanimate agents occur with ergative marking. Source: Casilimas Rojas 1995: 186

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comentario: When A is thematized (fronted to pre-verbal position), the ergative marker is OBLIGATORILY removed (Bril 2002: §3.7.1, p.57: 'Le sujet thématisé du verbe transitif apparaît sans les marques d'agent an ou ru'). Corrected from original annotation 1→0. Source: Bril 2002: 57

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comentario: No topicality-based split is documented in Merlan and Rumsey (1991). The optional dropping of -n(i) is conditioned by phonological/discourse factors, not by the topicality of A per se. Topical A retains ergative marking. Changed from original annotation '?' to 1. Source: Merlan and Rumsey 1991: 337-339

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comentario: No topicality-based split documented. Non-topical A takes ergative marking as expected. Changed from original annotation '?' to 1. Source: Merlan and Rumsey 1991: 337-339

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comentario: All persons of pronouns have distinct ergative/agentive forms with le³³ in Dechang dialect of Lisu. Confirmed in Yu (2007). Changed from original annotation '?'→1. Source: Yu 2007: cap. 3

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comentario: All persons of pronouns have distinct ergative/agentive forms with le³³. Changed from original annotation '?'→1. Source: Yu 2007: cap. 3

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comentario: All persons of pronouns have distinct ergative/agentive forms with le³³. Changed from original annotation '?'→1. Source: Yu 2007: cap. 3

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comentario: Non-agentive intransitive S (So) takes zero marking (absolutive), not le³³. The active-stative system distinguishes Sa (agentive, takes le³³) from So (non-agentive, zero). Changed from original annotation '?'→0. Source: Yu 2007: cap. 4

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comentario: CORRECTED from original annotation 1→0. In the active-stative system, the conditioning factor is agentivity/control, not topicality. See example (3a-b): the split is between Sa and So, not between topical and non-topical A. Topicality does not systematically condition the presence/absence of le³³. Source: Yu 2007: 82

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comentario: Inanimate A: original annotation 0 lacks specific citation for Dechang; Yu (2007) does not explicitly address inanimate agents for this dialect. Changed from original annotation 0→? (insufficient evidence). Source: Yu 2007: in passim

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: CORRECTED from original annotation '?'→0. In Dechang dialect, nɛ³³ is the LOCATIVE marker (Yu 2007), not the instrumental. The ergative/agentive marker is le³³; instrumental is du³³. ERG≠INST. Source: Yu 2007: cap. 4

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comentario: Perfective/imperfective aspect is not a morphological category in Dharumbal; tense categories are Non-Past, Past, Far-Past (Terrill §5.1). Source: Terrill 2002: in passim

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comentario: Perfective/imperfective aspect is not a morphological category in Dharumbal. Source: Terrill 2002: in passim

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comentario: Realis/irrealis is not a morphological category in Dharumbal; tense/mood system has no such distinction. Source: Terrill 2002: in passim

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comentario: Realis/irrealis is not a morphological category in Dharumbal. Source: Terrill 2002: in passim

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comentario: No topicality conditioning of ergative marking described or evidenced anywhere in Terrill (2002); consistent ERG system applies to topical A. Source: Terrill 2002: in passim

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comentario: No topicality conditioning; consistent ERG system applies to non-topical A. Source: Terrill 2002: in passim

Descripción_rasgo: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comentario: The 'unknown conditioning' in Terrill §4.1.3 refers to the overt accusative marker -(n)a on human O (object), not to any conditioning of ERG marking on A. The ERG suffix itself is regular and conditioned only by phonology. Source: Terrill 2002: 31

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comentario: Continuative/imperfective aspect (-pa) co-occurs with ERG marking: yomo'is tyonvitu'yajpa 'The women turn the tortillas' (§2.1.2). No aspect-based split. Source: Engel & Bartholomew 1987: 341 (§2.1.2)

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comentario: Present/continuative and future contexts also show ERG -'is. No tense-based split. Source: Engel & Bartholomew 1987: 341, 383

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comentario: ERG -'is applies in subordinate and modal contexts (§11.3, §15.2); participial relative clauses explicitly require -'is on transitive subjects (§15.2.1). Source: Engel & Bartholomew 1987: §11.3, §15.2

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comentario: Future (manba), conditional (oca si), and purpose clauses (va'co) also show ERG -'is on transitive subjects. Source: Engel & Bartholomew 1987: §11.1.4, §11.3.3

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comentario: Causative prefix yac- creates transitive constructions with non-volitional/inanimate causers taking ERG -'is (sava'is = wind-ERG, p.344). ERG applies to non-agentive A. Source: Engel & Bartholomew 1987: 344 (causative constructions)

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comentario: No topicality conditioning; ERG applies equally to non-topical A. Source: Engel & Bartholomew 1987: 373

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comentario: Participial/relative clauses explicitly documented: 'Si el elemento de relativo es el sujeto del verbo transitivo... se une el sufijo ergativo -'is al verbo' (§15.2.1, p.401). Source: Engel & Bartholomew 1987: 401 (§15.2.1)

Descripción_rasgo: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comentario: No additional conditioning beyond the person-based split (1st/2nd: verb agreement only; 3rd/NP: nominal suffix -'is). This split is already captured in GB409_2-3. Source: Engel & Bartholomew 1987: 344

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: ERG suffix -'is also marks possessors (§2.2.1, p.342: 'El sustantivo poseedor lleva el sufijo ergativo'). Explicit ERG=GEN syncretism. Source: Engel & Bartholomew 1987: 342 (§2.2.1)

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Instrumental/comitative expressed through postpositions (-pit 'with', -ji'n 'with', §5, pp.356-357), entirely distinct from ERG suffix -'is. Source: Engel & Bartholomew 1987: 356-357

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comentario: Ergative alignment is consistent across tense contexts in Wobzi Khroskyabs; no tense-based split is documented in Lai (2017). Source: Lai, 2017

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comentario: Non-indicative moods (imperative/optative) are documented with ergative marking in Lai (2017); no mood-based split found. Source: Lai, 2017

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comentario: Ergative alignment is attested in irrealis contexts in Lai (2017); no realis/irrealis split documented. Source: Lai, 2017

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comentario: No topicality-based split documented in Lai (2017); ergative applies to non-topical A as expected in a consistent ergative system. Source: Lai, 2017

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comentario: No animacy-based split documented in Lai (2017); ergative marking attested with inanimate agents. Source: Lai, 2017

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comentario: Ergative alignment is consistently documented in main clauses throughout Lai (2017). Source: Lai, 2017

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comentario: Ergative marking is documented in subordinate/non-main clauses in Lai (2017). Source: Lai, 2017

Descripción_rasgo: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comentario: The agent-prominence/voice system of Wobzi Khroskyabs constitutes an additional conditioning factor beyond basic transitive A marking, documented in Lai (2017). Source: Lai, 2017

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comentario: Typological inference for Pama-Nyungan; direct evidence unavailable due to OCR quality of source scan. Value is inferred. Source: Brasch 1975: in passim (typological inference)

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comentario: Typological inference for Pama-Nyungan; direct evidence unavailable due to OCR quality of source scan. Value is inferred. Source: Brasch 1975: in passim (typological inference)

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comentario: Case marking hierarchy table (p.147) explicitly shows NP[-hum] (non-human) in A position does NOT take ERG; they appear in the NOM column. ERG is restricted to human NPs and pronouns. Source: Brasch 1975: 147

Descripción_rasgo: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comentario: The humanness-based conditioning (human NPs take ERG, non-human NPs take NOM-ABS) constitutes an additional conditioning factor beyond the basic transitive A function. Source: Brasch 1975: 145, 147

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: ERG = -bo; no evidence of ERG=GEN syncretism in available readable sections of source. Source: Brasch 1975: 220

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Comparative chapter (p.220) confirms comitative = -gu, distinct from ERG -bo. Source: Brasch 1975: 220

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comentario: le³³ appears in non-indicative moods (imperative/optative). Confirmed from Yu (2007); changed from original annotation '?'→1. Source: Yu 2007: cap. 5

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comentario: Inanimate A: no clear examples found in Yu (2007) for Central Lisu dialect; inanimate entities rarely appear as transitive agents in the documented corpus. Value uncertain. Source: Yu 2007: in passim

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: CORRECTED from original annotation 1→0. Original annotation cited nɛ³³ as both ergative and instrumental, but PDF verification (Yu 2007) confirms that nɛ³³ is the LOCATIVE marker in Central Lisu, not instrumental. The agentive/ergative marker is le³³; the instrumental marker is du³³. ERG≠INST. Source: Yu 2007: cap. 4

Descripción_rasgo: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comentario: ABS is zero-marked in the singular (bare stem); plural -t is not a dedicated ABS marker (shared with common plural). No overt ABS case marker. Original annotation of 1 was incorrect. Source: Sadock 2003: 66; Fortescue 1984: §2.1.1.1

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comentario: 1st and 2nd person pronouns have a single 'direct case' (DIR) form for all grammatical roles (Sadock §2.11.1.2: 'The first and second person pronouns have only one form for all the direct cases'). No distinct ERG form. Corrected from 1 to 0. Source: Sadock 2003: 66 (§2.11.1.2); Fortescue 1984: §2.1.1.2.2

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comentario: Same as GB409_2: 2nd person pronouns use a single DIR form with no distinct ergative. Corrected from 1 to 0. Source: Sadock 2003: 66 (§2.11.1.2); Fortescue 1984: §2.1.1.2.2

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comentario: ERG marking applies in non-past (including future -ssa-) without conditioning. Source: Sadock 2003: 54; Fortescue 1984: in passim

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comentario: Sadock §9.2.1.6: 'the ergative marks the more agentive term of transitives.' Value filled in from empty cell. Source: Sadock 2003: 57 (§9.2.1.6)

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comentario: Fortescue §2.1.1.2.2: 'no distinction between agentive/non-agentive.' Even non-agentive subjects of derived transitives retain ERG marking. Source: Fortescue 1984: §2.1.1.2.2; Sadock 2003: §9.2.1.6

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comentario: Same: topicality does not condition case marking; non-topical A also takes ERG. Source: Fortescue 1984: §1.12; Sadock 2003: §9.2.1

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comentario: Animacy does not condition ERG marking; inanimate transitive subjects also take -(u)p. Source: Fortescue 1984: §2.1.1.2.2; Sadock 2003: §9.2.1

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comentario: In subordinate clauses (conjunctive, participial, dependent moods), nominal transitive subjects retain ERG -(u)p. Source: Fortescue 1984: §3.1-3.5; Sadock 2003: §9.3

Descripción_rasgo: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comentario: No additional conditioning beyond the core transitive subject function. Person-based split (GB409_2=0, GB409_3=0) is already captured in earlier features. Source: Sadock 2003: in passim; Fortescue 1984: in passim

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Possessor phrases take the same ERG/relative case -(u)p (Sadock §5.5.3.1; Fortescue §2.1.1.4.6). Explicit ERG=GEN syncretism. Source: Sadock 2003: 28 (§5.5.3.1); Fortescue 1984: §2.1.1.4.6

Descripción_rasgo: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comentario: ABS is zero-marked; ERG suffix -lu/-ju is the only core case marker. Confirmed by McKelson Lesson 39-40. Source: McKelson 2004: 39

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comentario: 1SG takes ERG suffix -lu when transitive subject (ngajulu); bare ngaju for intransitive S. Source: McKelson 2004: 11, 39

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comentario: 2SG nyuntu takes -lu as transitive subject: nyuntulu kawa mayi walipikarti 'You take the tucker' (Lesson 5, p.6). Source: McKelson 2004: 6, 39

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comentario: 3rd person full NPs take -lu/-ju as transitive subjects: wakalalu jinkanu jurru 'the woman hit the snake' (Lesson 39, p.39). Demonstrative pronouns also take -lu in A role. Source: McKelson 2004: 39

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comentario: Full NPs take ERG suffix -lu (after vowels) / -ju (after consonants): wakalalu (woman-ERG), wilarrju (turtle-ERG). McKelson p.39-40 explicitly explains the rule. Source: McKelson 2004: 39-40

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comentario: Past tense examples in Lesson 39-40 show ERG -lu/-ju on transitive subjects (jinkanu = past hit). Source: McKelson 2004: 39

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comentario: No tense-based conditioning of ERG marking documented; -lu/-ju applies across tenses. Source: McKelson 2004: 39-40

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comentario: All declarative/indicative examples show ERG marking on transitive A. Source: McKelson 2004: 39

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comentario: All documented A arguments (woman, turtle, person) are agentive and take ERG -lu/-ju. Source: McKelson 2004: 5-6, 39

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comentario: All ERG-marked A arguments in examples are animate (woman, turtle, people). Source: McKelson 2004: 39

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comentario: All ergative examples occur in main clauses; ERG -lu/-ju consistently applies. Source: McKelson 2004: 39

Descripción_rasgo: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comentario: McKelson (p.39) states: 'lu and ju indicate an object-affecting subject' — a simple categorical rule with no additional conditioning mentioned. Source: McKelson 2004: 39

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Genitive/possessive = -kura (Lesson 7, p.8: japulukura 'father's'). Entirely distinct from ERG -lu/-ju. Source: McKelson 2004: 8

Descripción_rasgo: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comentario: Comitative = pari 'with' (Lesson 14, p.15: warnku pari 'with money'). Entirely distinct from ERG -lu/-ju. Source: McKelson 2004: 14-15

Descripción_rasgo: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comentario: Non-agentive A takes ergative marking in Series II. Hewitt (1990, pp.187-189) provides multiple examples of inanimate/abstract agents with no volitional control taking the ergative case: sun-ERG (dried the field), sweat-ERG (penetrated the shirt), pleasure-ERG (made me dizzy), God-ERG (let you grow old), illness-ERG (weakened the man’s knees). These are Series II constructions and therefore take the ergative. Original annotation (value=0) was a coding error directly contradicted by the examples cited in the same comment. Source: Hewitt:1990, 187-189
